Business E2E map: Bunkai TMS

Generated 2026-11-13 from upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging 63d5e7e3 (routes, pages, components, role checks), the business data and API maps of the same date, and the legacy feature map, personas and journeys (August 2026) as input. Journeys first, then the feature catalog.

Who uses Bunkai and the journeys that carry it

Bunkai is a test-management web app. People reach it in the browser (Supabase session cookie); machines (CLI tools, AI agents, CI) reach the same /api/v1 with a Bearer personal access token. Five personas follow from the code: four workspace roles (workspace_members.role: owner, admin, member, viewer) and the machine caller, whose limits are token scopes, not a role.

Paths in this map are relative to the product repo upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging 63d5e7e3 unless they start with tests/ (this QA repo). Data and API detail behind each step live in business-data-context and business-api-context; this map cites their section ids instead of restating them.

Role hierarchy

viewer ⊂ member ⊂ admin ⊂ owner. The owner is the workspace creator, exactly one per workspace, and is never invite-assignable (invites carry viewer, member or admin). Since BK-572 (migration 0114, ADR-0022) the hierarchy is also a removal ladder enforced in RLS: a caller can remove only lower-ranked members, and nobody removes the owner. A browser session implicitly holds all four capabilities (atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin), so for people the real limits are the live role checks and RLS; a PAT holds only the scopes it was minted with.

The journeys that carry the product

  • First workspace (journey-first-workspace): sign-up with a mandatory OTP, then the onboarding form creates the workspace. Every other journey depends on it.
  • Backlog import (journey-backlog-import): owner or admin connects the workspace Jira, a member imports stories and acceptance criteria into a project.
  • ATC authoring (journey-atc-authoring): a member writes Acceptance Test Cases that must anchor to a story and its criteria, then maintains them (edit, bulk edit, archive).
  • Manual run (journey-manual-run): a Test is executed step by step with image evidence; a failed step becomes a bug. The highest-risk journey: it produces the evidence the product exists for.
  • Agent run (journey-agent-run): a CLI, CI job or AI agent signs in headlessly and streams or submits run results through a PAT.
  • Bug triage (journey-bug-triage), release sign-off (journey-release-signoff) and traceability review (journey-traceability-review) read and close the loop.
  • Plan upgrade (journey-plan-upgrade), team access (journey-team-access) and workspace exit (journey-workspace-exit) are the owner journeys where money, access and data change hands.

Goals

  • Stand up a workspace and bring the team in with the right roles.
  • Connect the team Jira so stories arrive without retyping.
  • Pay for the Cloud plan when the free limits are reached, keep the payment method and invoices in order.
  • Control the exit: export the data, delete the workspace, restore it within 30 days.

Pain points (from the messages the owner can hit)

  • Plan limit: "Your existing projects are untouched. Creating a new project is blocked until the plan has room." (components/billing/PlanLimitBanner.tsx).
  • Checkout failure: "Could not start checkout. Please try again." (components/billing/UpgradeView.tsx).
  • Slug collision on the first workspace: Slug "<slug>" is taken — try another. (app/(app)/onboarding/onboarding-form.tsx).
  • Invites are not emailed: the owner must share the accept link by hand (business-api-context journey-invite).

Owner-only permissions

Checkout, payment method, billing details and renewal retry; data export; workspace delete and restore. The last two and export also require a browser session (cookie-only): an owner PAT cannot do them.

Goals

  • Run the team: invite people, remove lower-ranked members.
  • Own the integrations: the workspace Jira connection and each project Jira bug-sync destination.
  • Moderate: close any test plan, delete anyone's chat message.

Pain points

  • Billing is visible but read-only: edits are owner-only (can_edit false for admins, lib/billing/summary.ts). On a plan limit the admin sees "Ask <owner>, the workspace owner, to upgrade." (components/billing/PlanLimitBanner.tsx).
  • Cannot remove or demote the owner: the ladder in RLS refuses it (migration 0114).
  • Cannot export data or delete the workspace: owner-only.

Journey: first workspace (sign-up to projects)

Persona: any first-time visitor, who becomes the owner. Entry: / (redirects to /login without a session, app/page.tsx), a direct link, or an invite link. Features: FEAT-003, FEAT-001, FEAT-004, FEAT-007.

  1. /login: enter the email; check-email decides sign-in or sign-up (email-first-form.tsx).
  2. New email: choose a password, submit sign-up; a six-digit code is emailed. Existing email: password sign-in (FEAT-002).
  3. Enter the code; the session opens and a default-scope PAT is minted (POST /api/v1/auth/confirm). Alternatives: magic link (FEAT-001) or GitHub/Google OAuth (FEAT-004), both through /auth/callback.
  4. A signed-in user with no workspace is sent to /onboarding (app/(app)/home/page.tsx).
  5. Fill name and slug, submit: POST /api/v1/workspaces runs bunkai_bootstrap_workspace (workspace plus owner membership in one transaction; a trigger creates the general chat channel).
  6. "Workspace created", then /projects (onboarding-form.tsx).

Journey: backlog import from Jira

Personas: owner or admin (connection), member (import). Entry: /settings/jira (owner and admin only in the settings nav), then the "Import from Jira" dialog of a project. Features: FEAT-062, FEAT-063.

  1. Owner or admin saves site URL, email and API token in /settings/jira. The token is write-only and goes to Supabase Vault; saving does not call Jira.
  2. Test the connection: Bunkai contacts only https://*.atlassian.net; the answer is ok: true or ok: false (a failed test is still a 200).
  3. A member opens the import dialog of a project and starts the import: POST /api/v1/imports answers 202 with a job id.
  4. A background task (Vercel after()) pages Jira, converts descriptions from Atlassian Document Format, extracts acceptance criteria and upserts stories and criteria.
  5. The dialog polls GET /api/v1/imports/{id} and reports "Import completed" or "Import failed"; it can be closed while the job keeps running ("Close (keeps running)").
  6. The member continues in journey-atc-authoring.

Journey: ATC authoring and maintenance

Persona: member (also owner, admin, agent with atc:write). Entry: the project explorer (/projects/[projectSlug]) or the workspace ATC Library (/atcs). Features: FEAT-016, FEAT-017, FEAT-018, FEAT-065, FEAT-066, FEAT-067.

  1. Pick a story with at least one active acceptance criterion; optionally mark it ready_to_test (refused with zero active criteria, FEAT-014).
  2. Open /projects/[projectSlug]/atcs/new: name, module, layer (UI, API, Unit), priority, technique, steps and assertions, and the criteria it covers (anchoring panel).
  3. Save: POST /api/v1/atcs runs bunkai_create_atc (ATC, steps, assertions and criterion links in one transaction); the editor opens the new ATC (/projects/[projectSlug]/atcs/[atcId]).
  4. Edit later: the usage panel shows how many Tests the change affects (FEAT-022, FEAT-023).
  5. Maintain in bulk: select ATCs in the project list and change one field on up to 200 at once; a report lists each outcome (FEAT-065).
  6. Retire: archive from the project surfaces with a usage warning; archived ATCs are read-only, listed in the ATC Library and restorable (FEAT-066).

Journey: manual run, evidence and bug

Persona: member (also owner, admin). Entry: a Test detail page (/projects/[projectSlug]/tests/[testId], "Start run"). Features: FEAT-025, FEAT-029, FEAT-030, FEAT-069, FEAT-034, FEAT-031, FEAT-046.

  1. Assemble the Test first if needed: /tests/new, pick ATCs into an ordered chain (FEAT-025).
  2. Start run, choose an environment of the project: POST /api/v1/runs with an Idempotency-Key; Bunkai snapshots the chain into run ATCs and run steps; the runner opens at /projects/[projectSlug]/runs/[runId].
  3. Mark each step passed, failed, blocked or skipped, in any order, with an optional observation ("What did you observe?").
  4. Attach images: init, upload the bytes to a signed Storage URL, commit. The image is visible only after commit.
  5. Finish with a verdict (passed or failed): untouched steps become skipped, run.finished lands in the activity log and notifies subscribers. Or abort with a reason.
  6. From a failed step, file a bug: only the run step is sent; project, module, run and ATC are derived on the server (FEAT-046).
  7. Later: compare this run with an earlier one of the same Test (/runs/[runId]/compare, FEAT-071).

Journey: agent or CI run through a PAT

Persona: machine or agentic operator. Entry: POST /api/v1/auth/signin (headless) or a PAT minted by a person in /settings/tokens. Features: FEAT-002, FEAT-005, FEAT-070, FEAT-029, FEAT-030.

  1. Sign in headlessly: the response carries a session and a PAT with the default scopes (never workspace:admin).
  2. Option A, streamed: POST /api/v1/runs declaring executor mode agent or ci, then mark steps as they finish; the run page shows an Agent badge and a waiting state.
  3. Option B, one shot: POST /api/v1/runs/submissions with the results keyed by chain position; the run is created already finished. A retried submission returns the same run.
  4. People read the result on the run page and in the project run report, which totals runs per executor mode.

Journey: release sign-off with test plans and milestones

Journey: plan upgrade and renewal

Persona: owner (admins see the billing page read-only). Entry: Settings, Billing (owner and admin in the nav), or the plan-limit banner. Features: FEAT-078, FEAT-079, FEAT-080, FEAT-081, FEAT-061.

  1. /settings/billing shows plan, seats, projects and retention against the plan limits.
  2. /settings/billing/upgrade: compare plans, choose a seat count, "Continue to payment".
  3. Bunkai writes the checkout-session row before calling Stripe (one open session per workspace) and redirects ("Redirecting to Stripe…").
  4. The owner pays on Stripe Checkout and returns to /settings/billing?upgraded=1; a cancel returns to the upgrade page and releases the session.
  5. Stripe posts a signed webhook; the plan becomes cloud only when the payment is paid.

Journey: workspace exit (export, delete, restore)

Persona: owner, in a browser session. Entry: Settings, Data export (owner only in the nav) and Settings, Workspaces. Features: FEAT-060, FEAT-059.

  1. Request a data export; a background job prepares it; download when ready (one active export per workspace).
  2. Delete the workspace: soft delete, tokens and pending invites revoked, access cut for everyone including the owner, a notice email; the owner lands on /onboarding.
  3. Within 30 days, restore from /workspaces/[id]/restore: "Workspace restored."
  4. After 30 days a nightly job purges the workspace; the deletion record survives.

Cross-feature flow: activity, notifications, digest and chat mentions

Spans runs, bugs, chat and settings (FEAT-034, FEAT-048, FEAT-053, FEAT-054, FEAT-076, FEAT-077, FEAT-058).

  1. A run finishes or a bug is assigned or moved: an activity_log row is written; database triggers turn it into in-app notifications.
  2. A chat message @mentions an active member: that member is notified once.
  3. The sidebar bell updates live (Supabase Realtime); a click deep-links to the run, bug or chat message.
  4. Preferences pick the channel (in-app, email) per family: run lifecycle, bug lifecycle, mentions.
  5. Every day at 08:00 UTC a cron job emails each user their unread notifications through Resend; the email deep-links back to the panel.

Fails silently: a failed digest send leaves the notifications unread for tomorrow, and nothing tells the user. Test it through the digest log, not the inbox. Data: flow-notifications, integration-resend.

Cross-feature flow: plan limits across projects, billing and renewals

Spans project creation, the app shell, billing and renewals (FEAT-012, FEAT-061, FEAT-078, FEAT-079, FEAT-081).

PlanProjectsSeatsRetention (days)Price per seat
Community3530free
Cloud5025902400 cents
Enterpriseunlimitedunlimitedunlimitedcustom
  1. Every workspace starts on Community.
  2. Near the project limit the app shell shows "Approaching plan limit"; at the limit a refused create opens the limit modal and the banner reads "Project limit reached".
  3. The owner gets an upgrade path; anyone else reads "Ask <owner>, the workspace owner, to upgrade."
  4. A paid upgrade lifts the limits (journey-plan-upgrade).
  5. A failed renewal that stays unpaid past 14 days makes the effective plan Community again: the limits shrink without the stored plan changing.

Projects are the only resource with an enforced create limit in this pass (PlanLimitResource = projects). Seats and retention appear in the billing overview; their enforcement was not found (see discovery-gaps). Data: entity-workspaces, state-payment.

UI inventory

middleware.ts gates the prefixes /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity, /atcs and /workspaces; /login, /auth and /api/auth are public. The sidebar holds Home, Activity, Projects, ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics and Settings (the last three open inside the current project), plus the team chat and the notification bell.

Discovery gaps

  • Secondary test identities after the staging user migration: the suite owner moved to a new account and workspace (2026-11-13); whether the member, viewer and non-member identities are members of that workspace was not checked. Every persona test depends on it.
  • No admin test identity: rules that separate admin from owner (billing read-only, removal ladder, test-plan close) cannot be tested with the current keys.
  • Seat and retention limits: shown in the billing overview (5 or 25 seats, 30 or 90 days) but no enforcement was found; a comment in lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts mentions a "no-pruning clause" for retention. Ask the dev team whether exceeding seats or retention blocks anything.
  • Agent capabilities on owner-only billing routes and team chat: whether an owner PAT with workspace:admin can check out, and whether chat accepts a Bearer caller, was not tested.
  • Magic link across devices: the callback verifies token_hash (BK-400), but whether the Supabase email template links with it is dashboard configuration, not in the repo. The legacy map said the feature was reverted; the code says otherwise.
  • Project rename and delete, Test delete, test plan delete and milestone delete: no API route; a page may still write directly to the database. The legacy map listed milestone delete as available; the route now has only PATCH.
  • Member role change: no route found; whether an admin can promote or demote after the invite is open.
  • Command palette permissions: GET /search requires atc:read; whether results are limited to the caller's workspace and rows was not traced into bunkai_search_workspace.
  • Traceability non-disclosure (BR-052) is carried from the legacy map and not re-read in this pass.
  • Journey sentiment: no usage data exists in the product, so the journeys are ranked by business risk, not traffic, and drawn as swimlanes, not sentiment journeys.
